name: Grande cuisine
aliases: High French cuisine of the 19th century
region: Paris, and the courts of London, Vienna and St Petersburg
summary: The cuisine of the great houses as Marie-Antoine Carême wrote it. Four grand sauces form the base of a system. Pastry and sugar make a pièce montée that looks like a building. Many dishes stand on the table at once.

philosophy.core_thesis: Make cooking an art of order and show: a system of sauces on the stove, and architecture of sugar and pastry on the table.
design_principles: Derive each sauce from a small set of grand sauces: espagnole, velouté, allemande and béchamel.
Cook the stock first, and clarify it until it is clear as glass.
Build a pièce montée of sugar and pastry in the shape of a temple, a ruin or a fountain.
Dress each dish with hâtelets, a skewer with a truffle or a crayfish at the top.
Serve à la française: many dishes at once, in a pattern drawn on a plan.
Cover a cold dish with chaud-froid and aspic, and pipe a pattern on it.
Write each recipe in exact steps, and give each cut and each garnish its name.
anti_patterns: A sauce made without a stock
A plain dish with no garnish
A dish for one guest on one plate
Spice in the manner of the Middle Ages

plating.composition: Each dish is built as a symmetric shape on a platter: a main piece with garnish in a ring, and hâtelets in the top.
plating.plate: A large silver or porcelain platter for each dish, and a gilt porcelain plate for each guest.
plating.portion: Each guest takes a piece of 100 to 160 g from a platter of 8 to 12 pieces, with a ladle of sauce.
plating.height: A dish stands 150 to 300 mm high; a pièce montée stands 600 mm or more.
rules: Set the pièce montée at the centre of the table and plan the dishes round it on a drawn plan.
Coat each cold piece with chaud-froid, and then with a glaze of aspic.
Stand a hâtelet in the top of each large dish.
Arrange the garnish in a ring round the main piece, one kind in each section.
Keep the pattern symmetric on each side of the table.

pantry.rule: Build on butter, cream and veal stock, add truffle or foie gras to the dish of honour, and use sugar and pastry for the centrepiece.

technique.bases: A white veal stock, a brown stock, a fish stock, a clarified consommé, and four grand sauces: espagnole, velouté, allemande and béchamel.
technique.details: A sauce strained through a cloth, a coat of chaud-froid, a skewer with a truffle, a puff pastry of many layers, a sugar piece built on a frame of wire.

flavour.profile: Rich, round and layered: reduced stock, butter and cream, with the scent of truffle and the sharp edge of wine.
flavour.balance: Umami and fat lead; wine, lemon and vinegar lift the sauces; sugar stays in the pastry and the centrepiece.
flavour.fat: Butter and cream give 40 to 55 per cent of the energy of a sauced main dish.
flavour.seasoning: Salt, white pepper, a bouquet garni in the stock, and fines herbes and truffle to finish.

palette.strategy: Use white sugar and aspic glaze, the ivory of velouté and the brown of espagnole, with the gold of gilt, on a white cloth.

service.format: Service à la française: all dishes of a service stand on the table at once, in a pattern drawn on a plan, and guests take what is near.
service.courses: Two to four services of 6 to 20 dishes each, with soups, fish, entrées, roasts and entremets, and a pièce montée at the centre.
service.tableware: Silver platters, hâtelets, porcelain with gilt rims, crystal and a white linen cloth.
service.setting: The dining room of a great house, such as the Rothschild house or an embassy, with a cook of a hundred pieces on the plan.

dishes.dish: Pièce montée: a temple of sugar and pastry

positive: pièce montée of sugar and pastry
overhead view of a great table

canonical_works.work: L'Art de la cuisine française au dix-neuvième siècle

evidence.title: Design for a pièce montée, from Carême's Le Pâtissier pittoresque
evidence.credit: Antonin Carême; scan by the Wellcome Library, via Wikimedia Commons

emotion.target_response: Awe at order and ambition: a table that looks like a monument, made by a hand that has planned each part.

use_cases: a banquet scene of the early 19th century
a menu or a still life of a grand dinner
a sugar and pastry centrepiece design
avoid_when: the brief wants a light or plain dish
the brief wants a modern tasting menu
the brief is home or street food

modifiers.request: simpler, with fewer garnishes and plated courses
modifiers.how: Drop the pièce montée, serve each course on a plate in turn, and cut the garnish to two or three items.

modifiers.request: plainer, with fewer sauces and a smaller table
modifiers.how: Drop the sugar architecture, cut the sauces to a stock and a roux, and use herbs for taste.

sources.title: Ian Kelly, Cooking for Kings: The Life of Antonin Carême (2003)
